unlock.title: Unlock your vault
unlock.description: Your vault is decrypted in this browser with your master password. Passwords never sees it.
unlock.e2e: The master password and every key stay in this page and are forgotten when you lock, leave or after 15 minutes without use.
unlock.twoStepApp: Your account uses a second step this page cannot do yet; unlock in a Bitwarden app, or add an authenticator app to your account.
unlock.wrongCode: That code did not work; try the next one.
unlock.unavailable: The password server is not available
unlock.noAccount: No account on the password server yet
unlock.noAccountDetail: Open {{url}} and sign in with your company account once to set your master password. Then unlock here.
unlock.waitingDetail: You can open your own vault now. The shared vaults open once an admin confirms you.

vaults.title: Vaults
vaults.description: Decrypted in this browser. The server keeps only what it cannot read.
vaults.fromGroups: Shared vaults come from your groups in Identity.
vaults.membersChange: Members change in passwords.yaml or in Identity's groups, never here.
vaults.empty: No items here yet. Add them in a Bitwarden app or with New item.
vaults.pick: Pick an item to see it

item.copied: {{field}} copied. The clipboard is cleared in 30 seconds.
item.editsInApps: This kind of item is changed in the Bitwarden apps or the web vault, which encrypt it on your device.

admin.waitingDetail: {{names}}. Confirming gives them the organization's key, encrypted in this browser to their own key, so they can open the shared vaults.
admin.missing: {{name}} is not on the password server yet
admin.missingDetail: Its name is encrypted with the organization's key, so it is made from this browser. Its groups follow from the file at once.

health.title: Health
health.description: Shared vaults, checked in your browser. Leaks are looked up by the first five characters of a hash, so no password leaves the install.
health.descriptionNoLeaks: Shared vaults, checked in your browser. Looking up leaks is turned off in this install.
health.unlock: Health is worked out in your browser from the items it decrypts.
health.yourVaults: The shared vaults you are in.
health.leakFailed: Leaks could not be looked up
health.byTeamDetail: Share of logins with no problem

leavers.title: Leavers
leavers.description: When Identity disables someone, or they leave the groups of the vaults, they are removed from the shared vaults at once, with the list of what they could see.
leavers.unlock: The names of the items are decrypted in your browser.
leavers.planDetail: On that day the person is removed from the shared vaults, even while Identity still lists them. Until then, this page shows what they can see.
leavers.noneDetail: When Identity disables someone, they appear here with the shared items they could see.

reason.no-group: {{name}} left the groups of the vaults.

leavers.couldSee_one: {{name}} could see {{count}} shared item in {{vaults}}. Change the ones opened in the last 90 days first.
leavers.couldSee_other: {{name}} could see {{count}} shared items in {{vaults}}. Change the ones opened in the last 90 days first.
leavers.cannotOpen: An item this browser cannot open

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Shared vaults only; what people do in their own vault is theirs. Kept 1 year and written to the log.
activity.unlock: The names of the items are decrypted in your browser.

server.title: Password server
server.description: The shared vaults, their groups and the policies, as the vaults file sets them, and Vaultwarden kept in step with it.
server.fewKeyHolders_one: Only {{count}} person can open every shared vault
server.fewKeyHolders_other: Only {{count}} people can open every shared vault
server.fewKeyHoldersDetail: Owners and admins hold the organization's key. If they all forget their master password, the shared vaults cannot be opened again. Make a second owner in Vaultwarden.
server.noIdentityDetail: Set PASSWORDS_IDENTITY_URL and its token, so members and groups follow Identity.
server.noVaults: No vaults in the file yet
server.changedInFile: Changed in the file, never here.

policy.recoveryNote: Account recovery stays off, so an admin can never open someone's own vault.

sync.title: Vaultwarden
sync.description: Brought in step with the file and Identity after every change and every five minutes.
sync.changed: {{added}} added, {{removed}} removed, {{vaults}} vaults and {{policies}} policies set.

file.error: The vaults file has a mistake; the last good version is in use

settings.accountDetail: Your name, password, second factor and sessions.
settings.membersDetail: Who manages Passwords, and with which role.
settings.signinDetail: Identity providers and how people sign in.
settings.tokensDetail: Tokens for scripts, each with one role and an expiry.
settings.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of Passwords if you need this.

form.e2e: Encrypted in this browser before it is saved. The server never sees what you type.
form.name: Name
form.keptInHistory: The old password is kept in the item's history.
form.totpHint: The key or otpauth:// link from the site's two-step setup
form.totpBad: This is not a two-step key or otpauth:// link.
form.moreUris_one: {{count}} more address is kept as it is.
form.moreUris_other: {{count}} more addresses are kept as they are.
form.moveDetail: Everyone the vault's groups give access sees it, and it leaves your own vault. It is encrypted again with the vault's key in this browser.
form.noTargets: None of your shared vaults lets you add items.
form.deleteMine: It can be brought back from the trash in a Bitwarden app for 30 days.
form.deleteShared: It leaves the shared vault for everyone. An owner or admin can bring it back from the trash in a Bitwarden app for 30 days.
